 Kaitlyn McCormick USA TODAY NETWORK Nov. 16, 2026, 1:03 p.m. ET Hear this story Seventy-six million Americans receiving Social Security benefits and Supplemental Security Income will see an increased adjustment in the next calendar year.
 According to the Social Security Administration, the 2027 increase is 3.6 percent, due to a rising cost of living.
 Here's what this means for you.
 How much is Social Security payment rising in 2027? What is COLA amount?
 The Cost of Living Adjustment for benefits payable in 2027 is 3.6 percent.
 USA TODAY Shopping: Shop sales in tech, home, fashion, beauty & more curated by our editors. The SSA provides the following table for estimated average monthly social security benefits payable in January:
 Before 3.6% COLA After 3.6% COLA 
 All retired workers $2,095 $2,170 
 Aged couple, both receiving benefits $3,238 $3,355 
 Widowed mother and two children $3,932 $4,074 
 Aged widow(er) alone $1,936 $2,005 
 Disabled worker, spouse and one or more children $2,970 $3,077 
 All disabled workers $1,642 $1,701 
 What does the 2027 COLA payment mean for me, my Social Security?
 The easiest way to look at this increase is to visualize that for every $1,000 you receive in benefits, the adjustment will bring an additional $36.
 To check your personalized COLA payment, check your online notice through your my Social Security messaging center.
 If you're not enrolled in paperless notices online, you should receive a mailed notice.
 Online and paper notices should be posted and sent in December, according to the SSA.
 When do I get my first COLA check from Social Security
 The first month of Cost of Living Adjusted Social Security is January 2027.
 Because Jan. 1 is a holiday, this payment will actually be delivered Dec. 31, 2026.
 Kaitlyn McCormick is a Philadelphia-based reporter writing all things cost of living related for USA TODAY .
